Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. This will override the default, incorrect search path and allow the compiler to find the necessary files. The header files for `libhypre-dev` are located in `/usr/include/hypre`, and the headers for `libmetis-dev` are in `/usr/include`.

I have adjusted the `RUN` instruction for the MFEM build to include the `HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR` and `METIS_INCLUDE_DIR` variables. This change is scoped entirely within the Dockerfile as requested.

### Corrected Dockerfile

Please replace the existing Dockerfile with the corrected version below.

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish) for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, Git, and MPI library
# Also install METIS and hypre dependencies from system packages to ensure stability.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables for build and installation directories to keep the system clean
ENV BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build
ENV INSTALL_DIR=/opt/deps
ENV PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/bin:${PATH}"
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"

# Create the directories
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} ${INSTALL_DIR}
WORKDIR ${BUILD_DIR}

# Build and install MFEM from source
# MFEM is the core finite element library for Laghos.
# FIX: Explicitly point the build system to the system-installed METIS and hypre headers.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
           MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
           MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
           MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES \
           HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/include/hypre \
           METIS_INCLUDE_DIR=/usr/include && \
    make install prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    cd .. && \
    rm -rf mfem

# Set the final application working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the Laghos application source code (latest default branch)
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source for building
WORKDIR /app/Laghos

# Build the Laghos application
# We point it to the MFEM installation directory we created earlier
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR}

# Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path
RUN cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Copy the required data files into the parent WORKDIR as instructed
RUN cp -r data/* /app/

# Clean up build dependencies and source code to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /app/Laghos && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
        build-essential \
        gfortran \
        git \
        cmake \
        wget && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# This forces TCP communication over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disables shared memory mechanisms that don't work across pods.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_keep_fqdn_hostnames=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

# Set default command to show laghos help message
CMD ["laghos", "--help"]
```

    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV INSTALL_DIR=/opt/deps
ENV PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/bin:${PATH}"
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"

# Create the directories
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} ${INSTALL_DIR}
WORKDIR ${BUILD_DIR}

# Build and install METIS from source
# METIS is a dependency for MFEM
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    make config prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd .. && \
    rm -rf METIS

# Build and install hypre from source
# hypre is another dependency for MFEM
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} --disable-fortran --with-MPI && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    rm -rf hypre

# Build and install MFEM from source
# MFEM is the core finite element library for Laghos
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
           MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
           MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
           METIS_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR} \
           HYPRE_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    make install prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    cd .. && \
    rm -rf mfem

# Set the final application working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the Laghos application source code (latest default branch)
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source for building
WORKDIR /app/Laghos

# Build the Laghos application
# We point it to the MFEM installation directory we created earlier
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR}

# Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path
RUN cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
        build-essential \
        gfortran \
        git \
        cmake \
        wget && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_keep_fqdn_hostnames=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. This will override the default, incorrect search path and allow the compiler to find the necessary files. The header files for `libhypre-dev` are located in `/usr/include/hypre`, and the headers for `libmetis-dev` are in `/usr/include`.

To resolve this, we will modify the `make` command for MFEM to pass the correct paths for the system-installed `hypre` dependency. We can do this using the `HYPRE_OPT` and `HYPRE_LIB` variables, which are respected by the MFEM makefile.

-   `HYPRE_OPT="-I/usr/include/hypre"`: This tells the compiler to look for header files in the directory where `libhypre-dev` places them.
-   `HYPRE_LIB="-lHYPRE"`: This tells the linker which library to link against.

This change is scoped entirely within the Dockerfile and adheres to all specified constraints.

### Corrected Dockerfile

Please replace the existing Dockerfile with the following corrected version. The change is in the `RUN` instruction for building MFEM.

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish) for a modern, stable environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, Git, and MPI library
# Also install METIS and hypre dependencies from system packages to ensure stability and avoid source compilation issues.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables for custom build installation directories
ENV BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build
ENV INSTALL_DIR=/opt/deps
ENV PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/bin:${PATH}"
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${INSTALL_DIR}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"

# Create the directories
RUN mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} ${INSTALL_DIR}
WORKDIR ${BUILD_DIR}

# Build and install MFEM from source
# MFEM is the core finite element library for Laghos.
# Its build system will automatically find the system-installed METIS and hypre libraries.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
           MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
           MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
           MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES \
           HYPRE_OPT="-I/usr/include/hypre" \
           HYPRE_LIB="-lHYPRE" && \
    make install prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    cd .. && \
    rm -rf mfem

# Set the final application working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the Laghos application source code (latest default branch)
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source for building
WORKDIR /app/Laghos

# Build the Laghos application, pointing it to our custom MFEM installation
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR}

# Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path to be universally available
RUN cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Copy the required data files into the parent WORKDIR as instructed
RUN cp -r data/* /app/

# Clean up build dependencies and source code to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /app/Laghos && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
        build-essential \
        gfortran \
        git \
        cmake \

    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized/cloud environments (e.g., Kubernetes)
# This forces TCP communication over the primary network interface (eth0)
# and disables shared memory mechanisms that don't work across pods.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_keep_fqdn_hostnames=1

Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. This will override the default, incorrect search path and allow the compiler to find the necessary files. The header files for `libhypre-dev` are located in `/usr/include/hypre`, and the headers for `libmetis-dev` are in `/usr/include`.

I have adjusted the `RUN` instruction for the MFEM build to include the `HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR` and `METIS_INCLUDE_DIR` variables. This change is scoped entirely within the Dockerfile as requested.

### Corrected Dockerfile

Please replace the existing Dockerfile with the corrected version below.

# Set the working directory to the Laghos source for building

# Build the Laghos application, pointing it to our custom MFEM installation
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR}

# Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path to be universally available
RUN cp laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \

        git \
        cmake \

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. ```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. ### Error Analysis

The build process fails during the compilation of the MFEM library with the following error:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
   12 | #include "HYPRE_config.h"
      |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
compilation terminated.
make: *** [makefile:520: parallel] Error 2
```

This error indicates that the compiler cannot locate the header file `HYPRE_config.h`, which is part of the `hypre` library development files. Although `libhypre-dev` was successfully installed via `apt`, the MFEM build system is not automatically finding its location. The system package manager places the hypre headers in a subdirectory, `/usr/include/hypre`, which is not always in the default search path for build systems like MFEM's.

--- Dockerfile.old

Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. This will override the default, incorrect search path and allow the compiler to find the necessary files. The header files for `libhypre-dev` are located in `/usr/include/hypre`, and the headers for `libmetis-dev` are in `/usr/include`.

I have adjusted the `RUN` instruction for the MFEM build to include the `HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR` and `METIS_INCLUDE_DIR` variables. This change is scoped entirely within the Dockerfile as requested.

### Corrected Dockerfile

Please replace the existing Dockerfile with the corrected version below.

Hello,

As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library. The error message indicates that the compiler cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```

This occurs because while the `libhypre-dev` package was correctly installed via `apt-get`, the MFEM `makefile` was not explicitly told where to find these system-installed headers. By default, it's searching for a local, vendored copy of HYPRE within the MFEM source tree (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`), which does not exist in this build configuration.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we must explicitly pass the correct header paths for the system-installed HYPRE and METIS libraries to the `make` command. This will override the default, incorrect search path and allow the compiler to find the necessary files. The header files for `libhypre-dev` are located in `/usr/include/hypre`, and the headers for `libmetis-dev` are in `/usr/include`.

I have adjusted the `RUN` instruction for the MFEM build to include the `HYPRE_INCLUDE_DIR` and `METIS_INCLUDE_DIR` variables. This change is scoped entirely within the Dockerfile as requested.

# Its build system will automatically find the system-installed METIS and hypre libraries.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \

    make install prefix=${INSTALL_DIR} && \
    cd .. && \

WORKDIR /app

# Clone the Laghos application source code (latest default branch)

RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=${INSTALL_DIR}

# Copy the compiled Laghos executable to a system path to be universally available

# Copy the required data files into the parent WORKDIR as instructed

# Clean up build dependencies and source code to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /app/Laghos && \
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
        build-essential \
        gfortran \
        git \
        cmake \
        wget && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_keep_fqdn_hostnames=1
